title: Introduce regional subnet handoff, DNS handover, and least-privilege SG for private control plane
author: Emily Chen
release_notes: Adds regional subnet handoff flow, new Terraform module for DNS handover using conditional forwarders, tightened security groups for control plane components, upgrade/rollback hooks for controlled rollout. No API changes; operational impact limited to installer workflows.
description: Motivation: customers running Private Control Plane across multiple AWS regions asked for a consistent, auditable subnet handoff pattern and DNS handover so regional consumers can resolve control-plane hostnames without exposing a bastion or public resolver. This PR introduces a regional subnet handoff primitive in the installer, a DNS-handover Terraform module that configures Route53 Resolver conditional forwarders and outbound endpoints, and a least-privilege security-group layout for control-plane components. Changes include: 1) terraform/modules/region-handoff: new module that creates delegated subnet reservations, tags, and IAM role bindings used by the installer to hand off subnets to account teams; 2) terraform/modules/dns-handover: Route53 Resolver rules, resolver endpoints, cross-account role assumption guidance, and optional TGW hooks for environments using Transit Gateway; 3) security/sg-controlplane: split SGs to separate management plane, KV cache replication, and metrics egress with explicit allow lists; 4) installer/hooks/preapply and hooks/postapply: upgrade hooks that orchestrate DNS handover and validate resolver propagation before marking the apply successful; 5) helm/controlplane/values.yaml: small templating flags supporting resolver IP injection and allow-list annotations. Checklist: [x] terraform validate and plan locally, [x] integration test against a small multi-account sandbox, [x] security review for SG rules, [x] docs update for on-prem operator steps. Rollout plan: staged rollout by region using canary accounts; the installer will default to a non-destructive dry-run mode for existing deployments. Rollback: installer postapply records a reversal plan that can be executed by the new cli command 'installer rollback-handoff', the terraform state remains intact and the module exposes outputs to remove conditional-forwarder rules safely. Backwards compatibility: existing single-region installs are unaffected unless the new flags are enabled. Linear and context: linked to ENG-2345 for handoff primitives and INF-4127 for DNS reliability work. Notes and caveats: cross-account resolver handover requires the receiver account to accept an IAM role; documenting templates for automation in docs/private/vpc-dns-handbook.md. This description is intentionally concise but complete; see commits list and changed files for implementation details.
commits_summary: 8 commits: initial module scaffolding, Route53 resolver resource implementations, SG refactor to split management/data plane, installer hook wiring, helm templating, docs and e2e test updates, lint fixes, final squash and cleanup.
review_comments: Marco Alvarez: Please ensure the resolver endpoint creation respects existing NAT/eip quotas; consider optional creation flag. Author reply: added 'create_resolver_endpoint' boolean and documented quota notes.

Priya Nair: SG review: can we tighten the metrics egress range? Suggest locking to prometheus IP list. Author reply: switched to tag-based allow list and added an 'egress_metrics_cidrs' override for operator-managed ranges.

Samir Gupta: Concern about atomicity between subnet handoff and DNS forwarder creation; if handoff succeeds but DNS fails, downstream services could break. Author reply: implemented preapply validation and a guarded postapply step that either commits both changes or rolls back the handoff role binding.
QA (automated): integration test flaky once, reran and passed; noted in CI logs and test stability ticket INF-4231.
manual_steps: 1. After merge, run 'installer apply --region <canary-region> --dry-run=false --handoff-mode=regional' in sandbox account
2. Confirm Route53 Resolver rules appear in receiver account and resolve control-plane hostnames
3. Run 'installer validate-resolver --region <canary-region>' and wait for green
4. Promote to remaining regions using documented staged rollout in docs/private/vpc-dns-handbook.md
notes: This PR was coordinated with the networking team to avoid altering existing TGW attachments; added opt-in flags for Transit Gateway hooks. No user-facing API changes were introduced.
